questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. When you finish the turn, where should your car be?

options.text: In the center of the street
In the lane with the least traffic

questions.explanation: When turning left onto a one-way street, finish your turn in the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road under dangerous conditions
The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road under ideal conditions
The suggested speed on a road under ideal conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road under ideal conditions
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the fastest or slowest legal speed on a road under ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. Slow down in school zones, work zones, or when bad weather or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb on a two-way street, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your steering wheel to the left
Turn your steering wheel to the right
Rest your right rear tire on the curb
Leave your car six inches from the curb

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on the right side of a street with a curb, turn your steering wheel left and let your car roll back until the front right tire touches the curb. This prevents your car from rolling into traffic if your brakes fail.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Your vehicle blocks traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible
Wait for police before moving your vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Always identify yourself and help if needed. Do not leave the scene.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach their destination sooner
Follow the car ahead more closely

questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left
Signal and keep your wheels straight
Flash your headlights so other drivers will let you through
Drive around a car if it blocks you

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, this keeps you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in how long it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: How far ahead must you be able to see before making a U-turn?
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn where you cannot see 500 feet in both directions. Do not make U-turns near the top of a hill or inside a curve.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right. This rule applies to all intersections, whether they have signs, signals, or neither.

questions.question: Which is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up while entering a curve makes your vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch carefully for cross traffic.

questions.question: What should you do first when visibility is reduced?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly, reduce your speed first. This is your best response to poor visibility and dangerous road conditions.

questions.question: If convicted of driving without insurance, you must have SR-22 insurance for how long?
questions.explanation: Driving without insurance is illegal. If convicted, you must pay a $45 reinstatement fee and carry SR-22 insurance for three years.

questions.question: What should you adjust first before driving?
questions.explanation: First, adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your final seat position.

questions.question: What is a work zone?

options.text: Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.

questions.explanation: Work zones can be fixed in one place or moving (such as mobile striping, mowing, or snow removal vehicles). They are marked with orange signs with black letters or symbols. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to look over your shoulder to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles using this emblem are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: When can you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A crossroad is ahead. Be alert for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Be alert for other traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) does NOT depend on:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC.

questions.question: If a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
May no longer turn and must proceed straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer have to turn in the direction that the arrow indicated.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow, you should:

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Turn with the right-of-way. Oncoming traffic will stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop if you can do so safely. Do not stop if you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: Your vehicle takes longer to stop on:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on loose gravel or stones.
